name: Metoprolol succinate
mechanism_summary: Selective beta-1 adrenergic receptor blockade reduces heart rate, contractility and renin release. Oral metoprolol undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism, primarily by CYP2D6.

half_life_hours.source: FDA metoprolol labeling: elimination half-life approximately 3–7 hours, formulation dependent

v_per_kg.source: Published population PK estimates for metoprolol; illustrative apparent volume

bioavailability.source: FDA labeling: oral bioavailability approximately 40–50%; formulation dependent

ka_per_h.source: Illustrative absorption rate for an immediate-release oral dose

simulation_config.reference_note: Relative concentration-time visualization only. Extended-release products have different absorption profiles that this one-compartment model does not capture.

warnings: Do not stop beta-blockers abruptly without clinician guidance.
CYP2D6 poor metabolizers may have higher metoprolol exposure; clinical response and heart rate still require professional assessment.
parameter_note: Illustrative one-compartment oral PK parameters assembled from public labeling and population PK literature. This is not a validated PBPK model and is not suitable for dosing.

name: Omeprazole
mechanism_summary: Irreversibly inhibits gastric parietal-cell H+/K+-ATPase. Metabolized mainly by CYP2C19 and, to a lesser extent, CYP3A4. Omeprazole can also inhibit CYP2C19.

half_life_hours.source: FDA omeprazole labeling: plasma half-life approximately 0.5–1 hour

v_per_kg.source: Illustrative apparent volume from published PK summaries

bioavailability.source: FDA labeling: oral bioavailability approximately 30–60% depending on formulation

ka_per_h.source: Illustrative absorption rate; enteric coating delays absorption

simulation_config.reference_note: Enteric-coated and delayed-release products are not represented by this simplified model.

warnings: Omeprazole is a CYP2C19 inhibitor and may reduce activation of clopidogrel; this combination has an FDA warning.
Long-term proton-pump inhibitor use has clinical considerations that require professional review.
parameter_note: Illustrative one-compartment oral PK parameters. Active metabolites and delayed-release formulation behavior are not modeled.

name: Clopidogrel
mechanism_summary: A prodrug requiring hepatic activation, predominantly by CYP2C19, to form the active thiol metabolite that irreversibly blocks platelet P2Y12 receptors. CYP2C19 poor and intermediate metabolizers form less active metabolite, and CYP2C19 inhibitors such as omeprazole can reduce activation.

simulation_config.index_basis: Weighted CYP2C19/CYP3A4/CYP1A2 activity relative to a reference normal metabolizer, with no interacting drugs. This is a mechanistic index, not an efficacy prediction.
simulation_config.reference_note: The active thiol metabolite is not directly modeled. Platelet function, clinical indication, and bleeding/thrombotic risk are outside this model.

warnings: FDA boxed warning: diminished antiplatelet effect in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers.
Avoid relying on this simulation for decisions about antiplatelet therapy; urgent clinical questions require a clinician or pharmacist.
Omeprazole and other CYP2C19 inhibitors may reduce clopidogrel activation.
parameter_note: Pathway-index model only. No dosing, efficacy, bleeding-risk, or cardiovascular-outcome estimate is produced.

name: Simvastatin
mechanism_summary: Inhibits HMG-CoA reductase and upregulates hepatic LDL receptors. Intestinal and hepatic exposure is influenced by OATP1B1 (SLCO1B1) transport and CYP3A4 metabolism.

half_life_hours.source: FDA simvastatin labeling: elimination half-life approximately 1.9 hours

v_per_kg.source: Illustrative apparent volume for an oral statin; not a validated product-specific estimate

bioavailability.source: FDA labeling: low systemic oral bioavailability (<5%)

simulation_config.reference_note: SLCO1B1 is represented as an exposure modifier in a simplified manner. Muscle toxicity risk is not modeled.

warnings: Simvastatin has dose-dependent myopathy risk; interacting CYP3A4 inhibitors can increase exposure.
This simulation does not estimate muscle toxicity or lipid-lowering effect.
parameter_note: Illustrative one-compartment PK with a simplified transporter contribution. Not suitable for dosing.

name: Atorvastatin
mechanism_summary: Inhibits HMG-CoA reductase and increases hepatic LDL-receptor expression. Metabolized by CYP3A4; OATP1B1 transport affects hepatic uptake.

half_life_hours.source: FDA atorvastatin labeling: elimination half-life approximately 14 hours; active metabolites longer

v_per_kg.source: FDA labeling: apparent volume of distribution approximately 381 L

simulation_config.reference_note: Active metabolites are not modeled separately.

warnings: Statin-associated muscle symptoms require clinical assessment, not interpretation from this model.
parameter_note: Illustrative one-compartment PK; not a validated atorvastatin PBPK model.

name: Warfarin
mechanism_summary: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKORC1), reducing synthesis of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors. S-warfarin, the more potent enantiomer, is metabolized primarily by CYP2C9. VKORC1 genotype affects pharmacodynamic sensitivity.

half_life_hours.source: FDA warfarin labeling: mean half-life approximately 40 hours (range ~20–60)

v_per_kg.source: FDA labeling: volume of distribution approximately 0.14 L/kg

simulation_config.reference_note: PK-only model. VKORC1 pharmacodynamic sensitivity and INR are NOT modeled.

warnings: Warfarin has a narrow therapeutic index and serious bleeding risk.
INR monitoring and anticoagulation management must be directed by a qualified clinician; no dose is calculated here.
VKORC1 and CYP2C9 genotype interpretations exist, but this simulation does not predict INR or bleeding.
parameter_note: PK-only illustrative model. Pharmacodynamic effect and INR are explicitly out of scope.

name: Ibuprofen
mechanism_summary: Reversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 and -2, reducing prostaglandin synthesis. Metabolized mainly by CYP2C9.

v_per_kg.source: Published PK summaries; illustrative apparent volume

bioavailability.source: FDA labeling: rapidly and completely absorbed

simulation_config.reference_note: Renal and gastrointestinal effects are not modeled.

warnings: NSAIDs carry gastrointestinal, renal and cardiovascular risks that depend on many factors not captured here.
parameter_note: Illustrative one-compartment PK; not suitable for dosing.

name: Tacrolimus
mechanism_summary: Binds FKBP12 and inhibits calcineurin, reducing T-cell activation. Metabolized primarily by CYP3A4 and CYP3A5; CYP3A5 expressers clear tacrolimus more rapidly. Narrow therapeutic index.

half_life_hours.source: FDA tacrolimus labeling: highly variable half-life

v_per_kg.source: FDA labeling: volume of distribution based on plasma approximately 1.4 L/kg

simulation_config.reference_note: Therapeutic drug monitoring is essential in real care; this model cannot replace it.

warnings: Tacrolimus has a narrow therapeutic index and serious toxicity; dosing requires transplant-specialist management and therapeutic drug monitoring.
This simulation does not calculate a dose or predict rejection or toxicity.
parameter_note: Illustrative PK-only model with high between-person variability. Not for clinical use.

name: Levothyroxine
mechanism_summary: Synthetic thyroxine (T4) replaced for hypothyroidism. Absorption and dose requirements are influenced by many factors, but the pharmacokinetics are not primarily CYP-mediated.
warnings: Thyroid hormone dose adjustment requires TSH monitoring and clinician supervision.
parameter_note: No simulation is offered: a simplified PK model would not meaningfully inform thyroid hormone management.

name: Albuterol inhaler
mechanism_summary: Beta-2 adrenergic agonist causing bronchial smooth-muscle relaxation. Inhaled route and local lung deposition dominate; a systemic oral model is not appropriate.
warnings: Rescue inhaler use patterns and asthma control should be reviewed with a clinician.
parameter_note: Inhaled pulmonary deposition is not represented by the oral model, so no simulation is offered.

name: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol)
mechanism_summary: A precursor to calcidiol and calcitriol; supports calcium and phosphate homeostasis. Supplement decisions depend on measured 25-hydroxyvitamin D and clinical context.
warnings: Supplement use should be based on measured vitamin D status and professional guidance.
parameter_note: No PK simulation: the relevant biology is the slow vitamin D metabolite pool, not a simple plasma half-life.

name: Fluconazole
mechanism_summary: Inhibits fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase. It is also a clinically important inhibitor of CYP2C9, CYP2C19 and CYP3A4, and is renally eliminated.

v_per_kg.source: FDA labeling: volume of distribution approximates total body water

simulation_config.reference_note: Simulation of fluconazole exposure only; interaction effects on other drugs are flagged separately.

warnings: Potent CYP inhibitor; interacting medication regimens require pharmacist or clinician review.
parameter_note: Illustrative PK; not for dosing. Interaction warnings are curated separately from simulated exposure.

name: Paroxetine
mechanism_summary: Inhibits serotonin reuptake. Paroxetine is a potent CYP2D6 inhibitor and can increase exposure to CYP2D6 substrates such as metoprolol.

v_per_kg.source: Published PK summaries; illustrative apparent volume

simulation_config.reference_note: Exposure simulation only; serotonergic and psychiatric effects are outside the model.

warnings: Potent CYP2D6 inhibitor; combination with metoprolol or other CYP2D6 substrates may require clinical review.

name: Clarithromycin
mechanism_summary: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis. Clarithromycin is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor and can markedly increase exposure to CYP3A4 substrates such as simvastatin.

v_per_kg.source: Published PK summaries; illustrative apparent volume

simulation_config.reference_note: Exposure simulation only; antimicrobial spectrum and infection outcomes are out of scope.

warnings: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor; some co-administrations, including simvastatin, are contraindicated.

name: Rifampin
mechanism_summary: Inhibits bacterial RNA polymerase and is a potent inducer of CYP3A4, CYP2C9 and other enzymes and transporters, reducing exposure to many co-administered drugs.

v_per_kg.source: Published PK summaries; illustrative apparent volume

simulation_config.reference_note: Enzyme induction develops over days and persists after discontinuation; the simplified model does not simulate induction time course.

warnings: Potent enzyme inducer; multiple drug interactions are possible and require pharmacist review.
parameter_note: Illustrative PK; induction time course not modeled.

name: Amoxicillin
mechanism_summary: Beta-lactam antibiotic that inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis. Renal elimination predominates.
warnings: Penicillin allergy history requires clinical review before any beta-lactam exposure.
parameter_note: No simulation: infection-specific treatment decisions are outside POLIS.

name: Azathioprine
mechanism_summary: A thiopurine prodrug metabolized to thioguanine nucleotides that incorporate into DNA. TPMT and NUDT15 activity strongly affect active metabolite formation and myelosuppression risk.
warnings: Thiopurine therapy can cause severe myelosuppression; TPMT/NUDT15 genotype and blood-count monitoring are used in specialist care.
POLIS does not simulate thiopurine toxicity or recommend dose changes.
parameter_note: Simulation intentionally unavailable: active thioguanine nucleotide kinetics and toxicity require validated clinical workflows.

name: Fluorouracil
mechanism_summary: A pyrimidine antimetabolite. Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPYD) is the rate-limiting enzyme for catabolism; reduced DPD activity increases exposure and severe toxicity risk.
warnings: Fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy can be fatal in patients with complete DPD deficiency.
Dose decisions require oncology-specialist and pharmacist management; POLIS offers no simulation or dose calculation.
parameter_note: Simulation intentionally unavailable for this high-risk oncology context.

name: Irinotecan
mechanism_summary: A prodrug converted to SN-38, a potent topoisomerase I inhibitor. UGT1A1 glucuronidates SN-38; reduced UGT1A1 activity is associated with increased SN-38 exposure and neutropenia risk.
warnings: Irinotecan toxicity and dose decisions require oncology-specialist management.
POLIS does not simulate SN-38 exposure or recommend dose changes.
parameter_note: Simulation intentionally unavailable for this high-risk oncology context.
